items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: he was able to ... pick all these little things and play them in any key and put them together, like Ella Fitzgerald and Mel Torme a little bit.

ctx.x: Do you think that’s more up in your head than it is figures?

I just — a gift from God. I don’t know what else to say. And I never have to use it because I tell people, when I listen to Art Tatum, the only album I ever owned by him was “Piano Begins Here.” And I say it should be called “Piano Begins Here and Ends Here.” You know. I’m joking. But I don’t think there’s ever been a piano player like him. I mean Oscar Peterson is close. But for me, sometimes now he plays too many notes, both of them. I can’t do it, I’m just saying, my point with the students is if you heard me…

pick all these little things and play them in any key and put them together, like Ella Fitzgerald and Mel Torme a little bit. Maybe not as much as Bird you know. And that was the thing of the day. Sonny Stitt and a couple of people, they would play, you know, whatever it is, a classical piece [scats] I don’t know what the piece that was, but Sonny Stitt plays that. But Bird would, and I noticed Charlie Parker, I only noticed this about eight years ago, on rhythm changes, the first eight bars of rhythm changes,…
